To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the antibacterial activity of cecropines is not dependent on the presence of a helix, and that a hybrid peptide containing the hydrophobic segment of melittin, and the cecropin hydrophilic segments is highly active against Gram negative and Gram positive bacteria.
the length, hydrophobicity and net charge of cecropine A and its analogs are critical to antibacterial activity.
the antibacterial activity of cecropines and melittin can be maintained in hybrid peptides, and that these hybrid peptides can be non-hemolytictic.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel antibacterial peptides with a broad spectrum of activity against both Gram-positive and -negative bacteria.
the design and synthesis of peptides with antibiotic properties and with the elucidation of structure-activity relationships in the peptide analogs and hybrids.
the design and synthesis of peptides with potential use in the treatment of bacterial and fungal infections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cecropins, melittin and their analogs are highly selective in their action against bacteria.

the antibacterial activity of the hybrid peptides is not a simple additive function of the activities of the two peptides from which they are composed, but is dependent on a complex interaction of several factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the antibacterial activity of cecropines resides in a region that is 18 residues in length and that the antibacterial region of melittin is 13 residues long.
the antibacterial activity of cecropine peptides is not dependent upon their hemolytic activity.
antibacterial peptides are not limited to a single structure, but can be designed to contain different structural features and still retain the same biological activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the activity of antibacterial peptides is not a simple additive property.
the hybrid peptides have a better antibacterial activity than the parent peptides.
the antibacterial peptides can be made to be non-lytic by replacing the cationic amino acids of the parental peptides with neutral amino acids.
